statement:
Research objective: Measure whether players' free-throw accuracy in the final three minutes of close games differs from their own baseline, and whether any difference is a stable player trait.

Data: 2026-27 NBA regular season from 2026-10-20 to 2027-01-31 (development period), plus 2022-23 to 2024-25 seasons. The 2025-26 season is not provided. Fields: play-by-play actions (actionType, subType, clock, period, teamId, personId, scoreHome/scoreAway, shotDistance, xLegacy/yLegacy, shotResult, shotValue, description).
Unit of analysis to consider: free-throw attempts in close late-game situations (about 2133 expected in the development period).
What would count as a meaningful finding: A player-level difference that is reliable across halves of the development period and replicates in direction on validation data, or a well-powered null that bounds the effect.
Validation: claims are tested on games from 2027-01-31 to 2027-04-12, which are sealed until every claim is registered. Planned approach: Correlate player-level late-game deviations between development and validation periods; report the bound if the correlation is indistinguishable from zero.

Register at most three claims. Each claim needs an estimand, a direction, a pre-specified test with a pass rule, and an analysis script that runs unchanged on the validation data.
permitted_memory: full history (all 384 records); no record uses 2026-27 data
